extracted.intended_audience: poets, students, and writers interested in fixed poetic forms
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for composing a sestina — a fixed French verse form — specifying stanza/line counts, the required end-word repetition scheme across stanzas, and the structure of the closing envoi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stanza and line structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A sestina consists of six stanzas of six lines each and a three-line envoi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the defining stanza/line-count requirement of the form: six six-line stanzas followed by a three-line envoi.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-word set and repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: The end words of the first stanza are repeated in a different order as end words in each of the subsequent five stanzas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select six end-words in stanza one; those same six words must appear as the final words of lines in every subsequent stanza, reordered according to the pattern below rather than newly invented line endings.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-word permutation pattern across stanzas
rubrics_metrics.description: The patterns of word repetition are as follows, with each number representing the final word of a line, and each row of numbers representing a stanza:
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
1 2 3 4 5 6
6 1 5 2 4 3
3 6 4 1 2 5
5 3 2 6 1 4
4 5 1 3 6 2
2 4 6 5 3 1
Use these permutations to place the six original end-words as line-final words in each stanza.

rubrics_metrics.name: Envoi content and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The closing envoi contains all six words, two per line, placed in the middle and at the end of the three lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The usual envoi pairing pattern shown is: (6 2) (1 4) (5 3). In each envoi line, one of the six words appears mid-line and the other appears at the line end; across the three envoi lines all six words must be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhyme expectations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The formal interest of the sestina lies in the repeated end-words rather than in a rhyme scheme; rhyme is not required and many traditional/modern sestinas are unrhymed.
